rggi_history.fact: Discussions began in 2003; seven-state MOU December 2005; MA, RI and MD joined in 2007; compliance began January 2009; NJ withdrew effective 2012 and returned 2020; VA participated 2021–2023 within this sample.

rggi_elements.fact: Power generators of at least 25 MW covered; official annual participation composition supports the nine continuous states. Regional cap changed in 2014 and subsequent reviews.

rggi_pa.fact: PA rule effective July 2022 was enjoined July 8; all PA allowances removed before September 2022 auction; not coded as operating treatment.

pa_announcement.fact: Pennsylvania executive order 2019-07 signed October 3, 2019 directed RGGI-compatible power-sector rulemaking.

ca_start.fact: First CA compliance period January 2013; supplied fuels covered January 2015.

ca_authority.fact: AB32 enacted 2006; cap-and-trade one component of broad state policy portfolio.

wa_start.fact: CCA passed 2021; cap-and-invest began January 1, 2023, with first auction February 28, 2023; industry and utilities covered subject to scope thresholds.

or_history.fact: CPP adopted December 16, 2021, effective January 1, 2022; December 2023 invalidation decision; 2024 re-establishment rulemaking.

or_transition.fact: January 2024 official release said final invalidation would follow appeal deadline; do not treat 2024 as a full operating year.

or_scope.fact: 2022 CPP covered fossil fuels, including industrial use; electricity generation excluded. This is not equivalent to RGGI power coverage.

or_restart.fact: Re-established program first compliance period starts January 1, 2025, outside sample; tradable compliance instruments described.

co_rule.fact: Regulation 27 establishes GEMM industrial obligations for 2024 emissions, with 2025 credit issuance/auction; GEMM 1 adopted 2021. No power-sector RGGI treatment is inferred.

ma_overlap.fact: MA 310 CMR 7.74 adds a separate power-sector cap from 2018, overlapping RGGI.

cs2021.citation: Callaway, B., and Sant’Anna, P. H. C. (2021). Difference-in-Differences with multiple time periods. Journal of Econometrics, 225(2), 200–230.
cs2021.fact: Group-time contrasts and explicit aggregation motivate single-cohort implementation; the analysis does not claim to run their full doubly robust staggered estimator.

mnw2023.citation: MacKinnon, J. G., Nielsen, M. Ø., and Webb, M. D. (2023). Cluster-robust inference: A guide to empirical practice. Journal of Econometrics, 232(2), 272–299.
mnw2023.fact: Cluster dependence assumptions, CV1 and restricted wild bootstrap; cluster count is not the number of independent policy adoptions.

mw2018.citation: MacKinnon, J. G., and Webb, M. D. (2018). The wild bootstrap for few (treated) clusters. The Econometrics Journal, 21(2), 114–135.
mw2018.fact: Few treated clusters can invalidate both conventional and bootstrap inference; bootstrap is not a cure for a single regional adoption.

roodman2019.citation: Roodman, D., Nielsen, M. Ø., MacKinnon, J. G., and Webb, M. D. (2019). Fast and wild: Bootstrap inference in Stata using boottest. The Stata Journal, 19(1), 4–60.
roodman2019.fact: Null-imposed wild bootstrap and bootstrap studentization; this project implements its stated elementary algorithm directly, not Stata boottest.

roth2022.citation: Roth, J. (2022). Pretest with Caution: Event-Study Estimates after Testing for Parallel Trends. American Economic Review: Insights, 4(3), 305–322.
roth2022.fact: Pretest nonrejection does not establish parallel trends and must not select the reported estimator.

rr2023.citation: Rambachan, A., and Roth, J. (2023). A More Credible Approach to Parallel Trends. The Review of Economic Studies, 90(5), 2555–2591.
rr2023.fact: Parallel trends is an identifying restriction requiring sensitivity and substantive justification. No HonestDiD estimator is claimed or newly introduced here.
